PARIS — French troops have been operating in Ukraine in non-combat roles since at least the summer of 2026 to maintain equipment used by the Ukrainian armed forces and provide training, Radio France Internationale reported, citing several unidentified sources familiar with the deployment.
The troops are part of a structure called Volia, after a Ukrainian word that can be translated as “will” or “freedom,” the French state-owned international news radio said on Monday . Volia is headed by a French general, and French troops operating in Ukraine are deployed under the guise of the Gerfaut mission in Poland to train Ukrainian soldiers, RFI said.
France has supplied Ukraine with equipment including Caesar howitzers, Mirage 2000 jets and precision missiles, for which maintenance expertise is being provided by personnel from various French support regiments, according to RFI. The radio broadcaster said it’s not disclosing the names of regiments involved to ensure the safety of soldiers and those around them.
The United Kingdom has also reportedly deployed troops in Ukraine in non-combat roles. Two serving members of the British armed forces are known to have died in the country since Russia’s 2022 invasion, with the U.K. Ministry of Defence confirming both deaths as non-combat accidents away from the front lines.
The structure of Volia is “light and modular,” composed of small teams for short-term missions, and Volia is not a combat mission, according to RFI. France decided against sending civilian technicians because Ukraine is at war, the radio broadcaster said.
While France’s constitution requires the government inform parliament of a conventional force deployment outside the national territory, neither the National Assembly nor the Senate have been informed of the existence of Volia, RFI reported.
Meanwhile, TV broadcaster France Télévisions similarly reported on Monday that France has secretly deployed several dozens of military in Ukraine as part of Volia. The outlet said it had confirmed the RFI information, but it did not disclose how.

Women held 29% of biotech board seats in fiscal 2025 but just 8.8% of CEO roles, highlighting uneven progress across industry leadership spots.
Women are gaining ground in biotech boardrooms, but progress at the top remains slow. Over the past four years, female representation on boards rose 45%, while the share of women in CEO roles rose just 3.5%.
Board membership for women in biotech increased from 20% in fiscal year (FY) 2021 to 29% in FY2024, maintaining at 29% in FY2025, according to the most recent industry report from Bedford Group Transearch. The firm began tracking the metric back in FY2021 and reports all data by fiscal year.
For the most recent year, female representation among board chairs rose from 11.7% in 2024 to 15.6% in 2025.
Progress has been slower for the CEO spot, where women held 8.8% of roles in 2025, up only slightly from 8.5% in 2021. And the growth has not been linear, with women holding just 7.9% of CEO spots in 2024.
In other words, 91.2% of biotechs were led by male CEOs in 2025, down from 92.1% in 2024 and 91.5% in 2021.
Overall, female representation among all named executive officers in biotech hit 22.1%, the highest level recorded in the four years since Bedford started the report, with distribution varying greatly by executive role. But nearly a quarter (24%) of females in executive roles left their positions in 2025, up significantly from 2023, when the exit rate was only 5.2%.
Author’s note: The Bedford report uses “female,” a term referring to sex rather than gender identity. This story uses “women” because the report mentioned identification as part of its classification criteria.

Mercedes-Benz Rolls Out Hands-Free and Point-to-Point Driving on the American Market
11 photos
Photo: Mercedes-Benz
There are so many driver assistance solutions on the market right now that it is almost impossible to keep track of them all. And the list of such things is about to grow even bigger, as German carmaker Mercedes-Benz has finally decided to roll out hands-free and point-to-point assistance driving on the American market early next year.
Something called the MB.DRIVE Assist Pro is also on the table and is meant to enhance Mercedes' MB.Drive portfolio. In essence, we're talking about a SAE Level 2 system, meaning drivers will continue to remain responsible for driving and as alert as if they were doing it themselves.
But let's take things one at a time, starting with the hands-free driving solution. Designed to work at speeds of up to 85 mph (137 kph), it can only be used on eligible controlled-access highways – you'll have to check if that's available in your area.
And the way it works is by assuming driving responsibilities, working in tandem with the Digital Extra: Distance Assist DISTRONIC to make sure it can adapt to any driving situation that may arise. A subsystem called Proactive Lane Change Assist takes over lane changes, including to overtake a slower vehicle or to pick a lane to get off the highway.
The point-to-point driving system, on the other hand, enables the use of driver assistance features for the entire navigation route, from assisting with exiting a highway to driving on crowded city roads.
The MB.DRIVE Assist Pro solution can be activated by drivers by pressing a button on the steering wheel, and it can then help with merging into the correct lane, turning at intersections, and braking or pulling away at traffic lights, among others.
To make sure nothing unexpected happens, Mercedes-Benz packs into the vehicles that will use the systems designed above ten cameras, five radar sensors, and 12 ultrasonic sensors, meaning a total of 27 sensing components that allow cars to make sense of their surroundings.
Mercedes says that the hardware required for these systems to work is already included on many 2027 model year cars, including the CLA Electric, GLE, GLS, and S-Class. More will follow in a few months, as more 2028 model year cars come to light.
It's worth noting that these solutions will NOT be free of charge. Without mentioning anything about pricing, the carmaker revealed there will be flexible purchase options depending on the model year. The rollout of these systems can be performed over the air, and the subscriptions available allow Americans to choose periods from one to three years.
The first U.S. roads to witness the MB.DRIVE Assist Pro and highway assist in action will be the ones in California, where an early access program kicks off next month, in December. They will be available on the 2026 and 2027 CLA Electric sedan, the 2027 GLC Electric SUV, S-Class sedan, GLE SUV and coupe, and GLS SUV. The rest of the country is expected to get theirs early next year.

source_document.body:
A report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence says installed energy storage capacity across the U.S. has topped 200 GWh. The news comes as the two groups, in their “U.S. Energy Storage Market Outlook Q4 2026” released November 17, said 14.3 GWh of new capacity was installed in the third quarter of this year, bringing the total to 48.3 GWh for the first nine months of 2026.
The report was published during the RE+ event in Las Vegas, Nevada. RE+ is the largest annual renewable energy conference in North America and focuses on several forms of clean energy, including energy storage, solar power, and more. POWER is a supporter of the event and publishes a magazine supplement that is distributed at the show, with the articles available on powermag.com .
The groups on Tuesday said the recent midterm elections, which will give Democrats control of Congress in January, showed that American voters sent a clear message that lowering energy costs should be a priority for lawmakers. More than 300 solar and energy storage companies sent a letter to Congressional leaders earlier this month urging passage of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), a bill that would remove some of the barriers to permitting of energy projects, including renewable energy installations.
The groups said the legislation would accelerate the deployment of energy storage, which in turn would support the integration of more renewable energy such as solar, wind, and geothermal to the nation’s power grid.
“Voters made it clear that they want lower prices, and the growing deployment of energy storage is helping make that happen. We’re urging Congress to pass BAAJA to build out America’s energy infrastructure and put downward pressure on prices,” said SEIA CEO Tim Pawlenty.
Momentum for Energy Storage
SEIA, a co-producer of RE+ along with the Smart Electric Power Alliance (SEPA), has continually touted energy storage as a way to support the deployment of solar power. The report, in noting that the outlook for energy storage continues to strengthen, said the 2030 cumulative U.S. deployment forecast for storage has increased by 3.7% to 708 GWh across grid and behind-the-meter applications. The reports said the revised forecast reflects sustained industry momentum, with U.S. installations up 20% year-over-year through the first nine months of 2026.
The report said Texas led the nation in utility-scale storage deployment through Q3, adding 12.3 GWh of capacity. Arizona and California followed with 7.7 GWh and 6.8 GWh, respectively. Recent SEIA analysis shows that rapid growth in solar and energy storage helped drive down average wholesale electricity prices by 42% in Texas, and 51% in California, from summer 2021 to summer 2026.
Utility-scale projects accounted for the vast majority of Q3 installations, with 12.2 GWh deployed, followed by 1.3 GWh of commercial and industrial storage, and 746 MWh of residential storage.
Eleven states surpassed their previous annual energy storage installation records in Q3, even with three months remaining in 2026. The states include Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama, and Illinois.
“States are moving from targets to centralized procurements,” said Pete Tillotson, senior analyst at Benchmark Minerals. “Across utility mandates and bulk capacity contracts, energy storage pipelines are growing as a result of both investment appetite and flexibility requirements.”
Manufacturing of equipment for energy storage also continues to accelerate across the U.S., as companies work to comply with policies that support domestic production. Recent battery cell manufacturing facility openings in Tennessee and Indiana have brought total U.S. cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, according to the report.
— Darrell Proctor is a senior editor for POWER.

EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
Acura Back in F1 for 2026 Las Vegas GP, Replaces Honda Branding on New Aston Martin Livery
7 photos
Photo: Acura
This right here is a bit of a tradition, and it's nice to see it come back every once in a while when dealing with a Grand Prix on North American shores. It all starts with the Aston Martin F1 Team, which is set to run a special livery for the Las Vegas GP. Also new are the driver's race suits and helmets, which together with the livery will feature Acura branding instead of Honda.
So, during this race weekend alone, F1 fans will be able to see Acura logos in place of Honda logos on the cars' nose cone, engine cover and even the steering wheel (together with the previously-mentioned helmets and race suits). You'll also be able to see the Acura branding across the team's entire repertoire of racewear, meaning the cooling vests and underwear tops.
Don't get too excited, an underwear top is simply that fire-resistant, long-sleeved undershirt worn directly beneath the driver's outer race suit. It's got nothing to do with their underwear .
Now that we've gotten that vital piece of information out of the way, we should also mentioned that for the first time ever, Acura logos will be applied to F1 Academy suits, thus expanding the carmaker's presence beyond what the F1 drivers wear. Aside from all that Acura stuff, Aston Martin will run a special livery in Vegas, as previously stated, designed specifically for its partner CoreWeave - which is an AI Cloud platform.
For those who don't know, Acura's presence in F1 goes back more than three decades. For instance, from 1989 to 1992, Honda F1 drivers (including Senna and Prost) wore Acura-branded helmet visors at the Canadian Grand Prix and the U.S. Grand Prix. Meanwhile, Jenson Button and Rubens Barrichello both had Acura logos on their visors at the 2007 Canadian Grand Prix.
In 2021, Acura returned to Formula 1 for the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, featuring branding on the rear wings of the Red Bull Racing Honda and Scuderia AlphaTauri Honda cars - this meant that Acura branding appeared on the driving suits and helmet visors of Max Verstappen, Sergio Perez, Pierre Gasly and Yuki Tsunoda. Max went on to win that race in dramatic fashion, points that proved crucial to him securing his first-ever F1 title.
Photo: Acura Currently, Aston Martin are second-to-last in the constructors' standings with a total of just 7 points - all courtesy of Fernando Alonso . He brought home 4 points in Malaysia, 2 points in the Netherlands, and 1 point in Monaco. So his best finish was P8 in Sepang, which is actually quite impressive given how disastrous this season has been for the team. More specifically for Honda, because they seriously underperformed in the engine department.
Initially, the entire car was overweight and lacked downforce, but those issues were eventually resolved (more or less). Hopefully they have better luck next year.

Ford Custom Garage Can Hook Your Maverick to No Less Than 300 HP With Two New SV300T Packages
14 photos
Photo: Ford
The Ford Motor Company's Ford Custom Garage is like a factory aftermarket option, and covers no less than six of its most popular models: the S650 Ford Mustang, the small Bronco Sport and the big Bronco, plus three pickup trucks – Maverick, F-150, and Super Duty.
As far as the pickup trucks are concerned, it’s no wonder that only the compact unibody model and the F-Series gain access to Ford Custom Garage – the Ranger isn’t nearly as popular as these three among customers. Instead, the Maverick and F-Series each dominate their respective categories.
For the S650 Mustang, Ford Custom Garages offers the FP800S packages as Black or Bronze Edition variants; the big Bronco, depending on the year, gains a wealth of options, the little Bronco Sport has the Blue Free Wheeling Package, the Super Duty has the 2027 Proud to Honor Package , and the F-150 again has more than you can count, just like the Bronco.
As for the popular Ford Maverick unibody compact pickup truck, which sold no less than 42k units during the third quarter of the year for a massive 20.4% boost over the same period last year, it is officially joining the Ford Custom Garage party with the SV300T Black Package and Bronze Package. Each is a comprehensive visual and performance addition to the roster, by the way.
Visually, they’re both mostly the same, as the differences boil down to colors: they feature 20-by-8-inch Black or Bronze alloy wheels, matching wheel center caps, as well as black or bronze lug nut kits. The packages are offered solely on the 2.0-liter EcoBoost inline-four turbo engine , complete with a Borla sport exhaust in black or bronze, plus Matte Black or Bronze tailgate lettering, an Air Design front lower spoiler, hood and bodyside graphics in black or bronze, Maverick Lobo shocks, and more.
They didn’t forget about a stabilizer bar and bushing kit, an upgraded intercooler, and last but not least – a Turbo Upgrade Kit with calibration. Ford says the pack uses “components from Ford's higher-performance vehicles and adapts them specifically for your truck,” lifting power – as the name also implies – from the standard 250 hp to 300 horsepower.
The healthy increase in power also affects the torque rating – the new output of 300 hp and 350 lb-ft of torque is a good 50 hp and 73 pound-feet versus the stock ratings of 250 hp and 277 lb-ft. According to Ford, you need a refreshed 2025 or 2026 model-year Ford Maverick with the packages available on the XLT, Lariat, and Lobo models – though only the ones fitted with the 2.0L EcoBoost and AWD. As for pricing, according to Ford Authority, that’s $15,595 when ordered as a new vehicle.

This R35 Nissan GT-R Hood Is Made From Pineapple-Fiber Composite. No, Really!
15 photos
Photo: Nissan
Pineapple leaves have little value once the fruit has been harvested. Nissan and Japanese materials company FOOD REBORN (in all caps) have found a different possible destination for those leaves, namely automotive body panels.
The parties in question have developed an R35 GT-R hood using natural fiber-reinforced plastic made with fibers extracted from pineapple leaves, along with a manufacturing process that could give a new use to agricultural waste.
This development further addresses a less glamorous problem in the world of motorized sports. According to Nissan , some racing categories require teams to use sustainable natural-fiber composites when modifying exterior body panels. Suppliers of these composites, however, are very few and far between.
This, in turn, makes sustainable natural-fiber composites really expensive and the supply unpredictable. Nissan and FOOD REBORN see their new material and production process as another option for that market. And yes, their process goes beyond the acts of extracting fibers and mixing them into some resin.
Fibers extracted from pineapple leaves are turned into flat yarn. Next up, the yarn is turned into fabric. That fabric is ultimately used as reinforcement in the composite material, a resulting material that apparently offers higher tensile strength than conventional flax-based composites.
Care to guess who uses flax composites right now? That would be BMW, which is rocking flax-based natural fiber composites in both motorsport and in the M Concept Neue Klasse that previews the first-ever M with full-electric propulsion. Nissan has not offered any numbers or details about its testing protocol, though, so we don't know for sure if the pineapple-based composite is actually superior.
Tensile strength, in this context, is only part of the equation. Other areas where pineapple-fiber composites have to prove themselves include weathering, impact resistance, dimensional stability, fatigue, and production consistency, just to name a few. Under the current arrangement, FOOD REBORN is in charge of producing the material using Nissan's manufacturing know-how.
Photo: Nissan The Okinawa-based partner is a relatively young company that will celebrate its 10th anniversary in September 2027. It specializes in biodegradable materials and natural fibers, and its experience with pineapple-leaf fibers gives the Yokohama-based automaker a truly reliable partner in these difficult early stages of production. Nissan contributes the composite expertise.
More than 50 million metric tons of pineapple leaves go unused each year worldwide, giving the project a substantial resource to work with. Not every discarded leaf can enter the supply chain, though, so don't expect Nissan and FOOD REBORN to scoop up all those 50 million metric tons in 2027 even if they were to be given a monopoly in this regard.
The Japanese automaker further sees opportunities outside the automotive industry, with Nissan describing the material as being potentially suitable for sporting goods and similar products. According to the wider Nissan Green Program 2030, increasing the use of sustainable materials is one of the company's desires.
Nissan has yet to publish a lifecycle assessment or a quantified carbon-footprint reduction, yet everyone and their dog understands that a natural fiber-based composite is cleaner in every way than carbon fiber. With a bit of luck, this and other immediate questions will be answered later this week at the SAMPE Japan Advanced Materials Technology Exhibition 2026.
The annual trade event organized by the Japanese chapter of the Society for the Advancement of Material and Process Engineering in collaboration with the Nikkan Kogyo Shimbun newspaper will run between November 18 and November 20, 2026, at Tokyo's Big Sight international convention and exhibition center. The Nissan and FOOD REBORN booth is located in the East Hall.

2026 LA Auto Show: All-New Hyundai Elantra, Rivian, Acura, Kia, Honda and Not Much Else, Actually
11 photos
Photo: LA Auto Show
The 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show doesn't seem packed with novelties this year, sadly. At least the ones that do will shine brightly under the spotlight and on the catwalk with less competition.
As tradition dictates, the 2026 LA Auto Show will come toward the end of November to wrap up a year of automotive events, running from November 20 to 29 at the Los Angeles Convention Center. According to industry insiders, there will be numerous brands in attendance, from Acura and Alfa Romeo to Ford, Genesis, or GMC, and from Chevrolet and Dodge to Tesla, Toyota, and Volkswagen .
However, the list of novelties, so far, is quite thin. One of the headliners will be the new Rivian R2 , which is almost ready to come to the market with up to 656 hp and a 0 60 mph time of 3.6 seconds, but also with an EPA-estimated 330 miles of range. At the other end of the spectrum, not that the R2 is any slouch, there’s the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric with up to 1,139 hp, hitting 60 mph in 2.4s and reaching up to 317 miles on a charge.
Interestingly, the US can’t be free of the Chinese either - Beijing-based FullGood Motor, which you probably didn’t know was formerly named Songsan Motors, will debut in the US with a Summer 7 retro-styled minivan. We can’t get back to the Westerners yet because Hyundai is also going to take the headlines with the all-new 2027 Elantra and its 2028 Elantra Hybrid sibling, teased for their global reveal at AutoMobility LA.
Most likely the new Hyundai Tucson will be in attendance, too, along with the upcoming Ioniq 6 N. Its cousin Kia America will not premiere any new vehicle but wants to attract our attention with a new experience bringing Kia’s “Opposites United design philosophy to life” – and they will include a huge 49.2 by 19.7 ft. LED wall “and three additional hero stages, two of which incorporate freestanding LED displays.”
Acura also aims to impress with the Acura Nexera Vision that acts as a preview for the brand’s future design and brings to the show two-time US Olympian and Team Honda athlete ambassador Kaysha Love alongside the latest model releases – the 2027 Acura ADX Urban Spec as a representative of the new limited-edition Urban Spec lineup, which also includes the 2027 MDX and Integra, plus the newly launched 2027 Acura Integra Type S Heritage Edition that celebrates three decades since the US debut of the "DC2" Integra Type R.
Last but not least, we also have Honda, which joins AutoMobility LA and the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show the same way as Acura – with existing models rather than all-new releases. The interesting stuff won’t be absent, though, as the Japanese brand will again show the Honda Base Station Prototype, this time around mixed with the 2027 Honda Passport TrailSport Baja Chase, along with the updated 2027 Civic Type R and special products from Honda Racing Corporation USA like the Civic Type R HRC Concept.

Amflow Continues Their Cycling Domination With the UE Carbon Urban E-Bike – Very Enticing Price
25 photos
Photo: Amflow
Back in 2024, DJI, the drone manufacturer, would go on to do something that no one expected: they launched an e-bike system, promising to be the gear to compete with giants like Shimano and Bosch. What they also did was actually launch an entire lineup of bikes that would be equipped with this fresh gear.
The brand is Amflow, and while most of their bikes have been out of reach for the common folk, Amflow just launched their urban commuter, and if I may, they’re really outdoing themselves , yet again.
When Amflow first showed its teeth in 2024, most people couldn’t fathom that a drone manufacturer just spat out full-suspension e-MTBS that could literally compete, even surpass most of what the market had to offer at the time. These babies were equipped with the Avinox, sitting as a perfectly tuned ride for what the Chinese powerhouse was bringing to the table.
Photo: Amflow Well, one trait of the Amflow lineup that kept most people away from the bikes was, sadly, price, or maybe it was the fact that not everyone rides MTBs. So, since 2024, we’ve started to see a sort of progression in terms of pricing for the Amflow beasts, but also the disciplines that their lineup can meet.
While it’s always been the e-MTBs that made the Amflow brand shine, over the past two years, they’ve stepped into adventure biking, whipping up the TL Carbon, a bike that can be found at as low as $3,900, and now, Amflow has unveiled their urban-destined ride, one that is perfectly tuned for the urban landscape and also equipped with the brand’s latest generation Avinox M2 system.
It’s called the Amflow UE Carbon and it’s this brand’s completion of the cycling practices that most riders today are undertaking. Sure, a road bike is missing, but hey, with just two years under their belt, Amflow is already on its third cycling discipline, and I can foresee a road bike in the near future; this is just an assumption and Amflow has not released any word of an electric road bike.
Photo: Amflow As for the UE, this is a whole lot of bike to talk about, and please don’t persecute me for summing up five pages of text into just 10 minutes or so of reading time, but we will be diving waaaaay deeper into an UE since we’re currently testing one as we speak.
For the time being, however, there are a few things that you need to know about this two-wheeler, and the first and most important is the backbone or the frame. At it’s core, the UE is built with a fully carbon fiber frame, one that weighs just 2.35 kg (5.18 lbs).
As we can see, that frame has been optimized for urban use, granting us access to a low-step structure which is essential for comfort and control, especially when you’re riding around with cargo on the front and rear. Amflow has unveiled images with the rear of the UE carrying a child, and the low-step is crucial in ensuring you tip the bike as little as possible during mounting and dismounting.
Photo: Amflow More on the comfort side, a dropper post is available and the handlebar, although not my favorite style, is a sweep-back (gull-wing) one, so very European. This does place the rider in a more upright position, and if I may offer a bit of insight, the riding I’ve done so far with this model has revealed that it is one of the most relaxing postures my body has assumed on an urban bike in some time.
Currently, the frame is a one-size-fits-all, capable of meeting the needs of riders as short as 5 ft 1 in (155 cm) to as much as 6 ft 3 in (190 cm), and does so by supplying riders with two stem lengths that can be easily interchanged and a feature which you’ll read about in the next paragraph.
More on the comfort side of the story, Amflow has decided to add a suspension fork to the UE, granting access to 65 mm of travel and equipped with adjustable damper and lockout. Don’t forget about the dropper post, which, aside from the adjustability, also offer 40 mm of travel to soften up the rear end.
Photo: Amflow Softening up also comes about with the help of Maxxis tires with 2 inches of cross-section, a trait that tells us that the UE can also break the limits of city use and venture onto gravel and hard-pack dirt roads. Magura brakes handle stopping power.
Oh, and you can do all this loaded to the brim with cargo since you have the Avinox M2 motor by your side, assisting us with 125 Nm (92 lb-ft) of torque, suitable for hill grades of up to 30% and is chock-full of hardware and software that constantly analyzes “pedaling intent” to offer the perfect power delivery when you need it.
Keep in mind that all these parameters are adjustable through the Ride app, and while the UE is available in two variations, the standard and Pro, both can tap into fully automatic and electronic shifting. The Pro is powered by a three-speed internal gearbox with the name Avinox on it and a Gates transmission, while the standard is rocking a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed hand-in-hand with TRP.
Photo: Amflow As for speed limits, well, the bikes will clearly be limited to the region where it’s being sold, even though it offers a peak of 1,100 W and the torque I mentioned. Keep in mind that the motor spits our just 45 decibels while under operation, and if I may, it really is whisper quiet.
This brings us to the last few topics on our list today. The first is range, a number which is highly debatable but which Amflow mentions can offer up to 82 miles (132 km) of ride time. With a fast charger, this one can be amped up again from 0-100% in as little as 2 hours and 23 minutes. All very notable traits, if you ask me, especially for a 600 Wh removable pack.
Up next, we have little tricks and abilities like the app I mentioned, which offers an insane amount of control over parameters, Auto Boost function, heart rate tracking, Apple Find My, and so much more.
Photo: Amflow Some functions can be tampered with via the touchscreen display, and we also have audio alerts in case someone’s trying to snag your baby, integrated lighting and rear-wheel lock, and the cargo racks. Don’t forget about the wireless charger that’s also available.
Last but not least, we have ourselves the most-important question of all: How much are we being asked to drop on this urban carbon fiber goodness? Well, remember that I mentioned that Amflow is aiming on releasing more affordable rides, with the standard UE selling for just $3,500 and the Pro for $3,900 (~€3,500). Not bad, if you ask me, and a price that some folks are sure to consider.
Drop your thoughts on this fresh beast below.

Audi R8 Drags R35 Nissan GT-R in America; It's Over in 7.95s, But Someone Was Sleeping at the Wheel
7 photos
Photo: Wheels Plus / YouTube
The videographer behind the ' Wheels ' channel on YouTube recently took a swing around BMP – aka Bradenton Motorsports Park in Florida for some cool action from the FL2K competition, then got back to The Strip, then switched again to BMP, and then went back to the Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway.
However, the related videographer behind the ' Wheels Plus ' channel on YouTube, who also usually dwells around The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway or MRP, which is short for Mission Raceway Park, aka Thunder by the River, from British Columbia, Canada, has decided to stay a little while longer at BMP.
So, over in Florida at the Bradenton Motorsports Park , we got to witness the clash between two of the coolest rides of the past two decades – the Audi R8, which has been around across two generations starting with 2006 and ending almost two decades later in 2024; and the R35 Nissan GT-R, the latest evolution of Godzilla, produced across a single iteration from late 2007 all the way through August 2025. These are two of the greatest sports cars of the modern age, and they’re well known for their performance levels, propensity to gain aftermarket transformations, and their unique engine sounds, among many other things.
As such, whenever an Audi R8 and an R35 Nissan GT-R meet at the local quarter-mile dragstrip, including at BMP, you never know exactly what to expect, since either of them or both could be tuned to become 2,000-hp rockets without anyone but the specialists noticing. So, while the Godzilla gives away its transformation via the long trunk spoiler and the parachute, don’t be in a hurry to dismiss the R8 before the battle ensues.
Surrounded by the members of their teams, the R35 and R8 carefully lined up for a perfect start and patiently waited for the green light. Alas, when the light came, it looked like someone was sleeping behind the wheel or taking a coffee break, since only the crimson R35 Nissan GT-R took off like a storm while the white Audi R8 lay pretty much dormant.
In the end, as the camera panned out to try to keep both in the frame, though that was pretty much impossible because the R35 was almost done with the race before the R8 caught speed, both decided it was better to cross the finish line. We don’t know exactly what happened to the Audi R8, as there is no additional information or context, and there is speculation in the comments section.
But one thing is clear: the battle was lost before it even began, as the Godzilla proved its worth to its team with a spectacular 7.95s pass at 176 mph, while the Audi R8 roared like it didn’t have a care in the world to a disappointing 9.65s result at an unknown trap speed. So, what do you think happened there?

Morgan Artisans' Proof, the 1-in-10 Coachbuilt Coupe, Takes Center Stage at Swiss Art Exhibition
71 photos
Photo: Morgan Motor Company
What’s your favorite era of car styling? Strictly from a visual standpoint, if you could have any – I mean absolutely ANY – car today built in a way that will make it look like it belongs (or comes from) another era, what will it be? To me, it’s the late thirties, and the flowy lines that were slowly gaining more and more appeal. Think of the Auburn Speedster, the Bugatti Type 57 Atalante, the Morgan 4/4. But, unlike all the other carmakers, the former hasn’t denounced its creed, even after nine decades.
Few automakers guard their visual lineage as fiercely as Morgan Motor Company, whose sports cars still channel the sweeping proportions of the 1930s. Arriving 90 years after the nimble 1936 4/4 established the marque's four-wheeled template, contemporary models retain those fluid, low-slung silhouettes, flowing front wings, and tapered tails.
Rather than chasing fleeting styling trends, designers in Malvern deliberately preserve the athletic grace and intimate road presence of their pre-war forefathers.
Equally uncompromising is Morgan's devotion to traditional coachbuilding, an ethos kept alive since 1909 at its historic Pickersleigh Road factory in Malvern Link, Worcestershire. Every vehicle leaves the production site entirely hand-built to order, shaped from English ash, hand-beaten aluminum, and supple leather by craftspeople whose skills pass down through generations.
By blending time-honored artisanry with modern engineering, the British marque ensures bespoke, human-centered craftsmanship endures in an automated automotive era.
Photo: Morgan Motor Company Morgan Motor Company will showcase its rarest contemporary coachbuilt creation, the Midsummer Coupé factory prototype, known as The Artists' Proof , at Sotheby's Zurich from 23 to 28 November 2026.
Staged at Sotheby's 3 Rämistrasse gallery, the curated exhibition titled “The Human Touch” celebrates perpetual artisanal mastery across luxury disciplines, pairing the hand-built British sports car with horological, high-jewelry, and collectible masterpieces that foreground soul over automation.
Designated Car 00, The Artists' Proof serves as Morgan's design benchmark, ahead of just nine individually commissioned customer vehicles, making for a limited series of ten examples in total. The project evolved from the open-top Midsummer barchetta unveiled in 2024 with Italian design house Pininfarina under its Fuoriserie bespoke banner, which was capped at 50 units.
After one collector requested a fixed-head two-seater , Morgan and Pininfarina re-engineered the concept, attracting eight additional enthusiasts in the ranks of the solid-roof Morgan owners’ club.
Photo: Morgan Motor Company Representing Morgan's first closed-roof production model since the Aero 8 retired in 2015, the Midsummer Coupé marks a milestone in the marque's 117-year history since its 1909 founding. Every example is handcrafted to order at the historic Pickersleigh Road factory in Malvern Link, Worcestershire, where traditional British ash-wood framing meets contemporary bonded-aluminum construction.
While official figures remain confidential, industry estimates place each bespoke commission comfortably above £250,000 before individual client specification.
Rather than simply bolting a roof onto the existing roadster, Morgan's engineering team developed a dedicated fixed-head architecture based on the company's latest CXV-generation bonded-aluminum platform. Billet-machined aluminum A-pillars and structurally bonded glass roof panels increase torsional rigidity beyond that of the latest Morgan Supersport.
Despite the added enclosure, curb weight rises by merely 2.5%—roughly 30 kg / 66 lb over a hardtop-equipped Supersport—keeping overall mass below 1,200 kg (2,650 lb).
Photo: Morgan Motor Company Underneath its elongated, hand-formed aluminum hood sits the BMW-sourced 3.0-liter (I should really use the British spelling, Litre, because it’s only befitting in this case) turbocharged inline-6 engine shared with the flagship Morgan Supersport 400 .
Tuned to deliver 402 hp and 369 lb-ft of torque (408 PS / 500 Nm), the powertrain drives the rear wheels through an 8-speed ZF automatic transmission. Paired with Morgan's lightweight chassis and double-wishbone suspension geometry, this mechanical package blends continental grand-touring ease alongside analog driver engagement.
Visually, Pininfarina's surfacing transforms the barchetta's silhouette into an expressive fastback grand tourer inspired by 1960s Italian sports coupes. At the nose, round fender-mounted LED headlamps with circular daytime running lights flank a tall horseshoe radiator grille with vertical slats, while concealed bumpers and a polished front splitter preserve clean aerodynamics.
Taller doors incorporate hidden handles within a crisp aluminum beltline, using fixed 100 mm quarter-lights alongside retractable drop-window glass.
Photo: Morgan Motor Company A central brushed stainless-steel spine runs longitudinally across the expansive glass canopy, dividing the sloping rear backlight into two panes before tapering onto a sculpted boat-tail deck. Single circular tail lamps punctuate the sweeping valanced rear wings above twin exhaust outlets tucked neatly beneath the lower valance.
Bright stainless-steel sill finishers connect the front and rear arches , framing 19-inch multi-spoke forged silver wheels wrapped in Michelin tires and bearing “Pininfarina” script.
Conceived in-house by Morgan's design studio under Chief Design Officer Jonathan Wells, Car 00 draws its atmospheric palette from the stark beauty of a Nordic winter. Its deep midnight-blue metallic paintwork appears nearly obsidian black in low ambient light, gradually revealing sapphire undertones when seen in hard sunlight.
Polished metal exterior brightwork, chrome-stalked circular door mirrors, and silver alloy wheels provide crisp contrast against the moody, sculptural coachwork.
Photo: Morgan Motor Company Stepping inside reveals a bright two-seat cockpit flooded with natural daylight from the overhead glass canopy. Soft ivory leather upholstery covers the sculpted seats, dashboard fascia, and central door inserts, contrasting with hand-finished, open-grain marine teak.
Beyond its visual warmth across the door rails, speaker surrounds, and center console, the natural timber provides acoustic damping that reduces panel resonance during high-speed touring.
Every interior touchpoint demonstrates meticulous metalwork and joinery, from the satin-silver door-latch bezels and black leather pull straps to a sculpted aluminum gear selector inlaid with teak. A turned-teak handbrake grip sits behind a slotted brushed-metal console trim, while three central ivory-faced circular analogue dials sit above tactile switchgear.
Full weather sealing, integrated climate control, and a roomy luggage compartment ensure genuine all-weather grand-touring usability.
Photo: Morgan Motor Company In Zurich, The Artists' Proof shares floor space with similarly rare creations curated by Sotheby's to illustrate cross-disciplinary mastery. Horology is represented by the Charles Frodsham Double Impulse Chronometer Hidden Seconds, distinguished by its crisp white dial, dark blue Arabic numerals, and blued-steel hands.
High jewelry features a Moussaieff Y-drop necklace uniting royal blue, violet, and pink sapphires with diamond ribbons, alongside a woven Hermès Mini Kelly Picnic.
According to James Marks, Sotheby's Senior Vice President and Global Head of Private Sales and Retail for Watches, these disparate objects are united by human ingenuity and uncompromising craft. For Morgan, which exports over 80% of its output across more than 60 global retailers while sourcing over 90% of components within Britain and over 50% from the Midlands, the Midsummer Coupé proves traditional coachbuilding is still a defining trait of carmaking.

REO Trucks Is Back, Reveals New $21,500 Pickup Truck. Slate and Ford Are Not Going To Like This!
14 photos
Photo: REO Trucks
Bad news is coming for Ford and Slate, the automakers rolling out affordable trucks. One more competitor will enter the segment. REO Trucks has come up with not one, but two trucks and an SUV starting under the $30,000 mark, with the most affordable being a $21,500 deal.
The Dallas-based startup REO Trucks acquired the brand rights and unveiled the digital designs for its Runabout lineup. Styled by Frank Stephenson’s design studio, the three vehicles are, as the company calls them, "Ameri-Kei" trucks, bringing together the compact body style and simplicity of Japanese kei trucks with American ruggedness.
REO Motor Car Company was originally founded in Lansing, Michigan, in 1905, by Ransom E. Olds after he left Oldsmobile. The first truck, REO Speed Wagon , arrived in 1915 as a light commercial vehicle, widely considered an ancestor of the modern pickup truck.
REO stopped building passenger cars in 1936 to focus entirely on trucks and buses. During World War II, the company built nearly 30,000 military vehicles, including heavy-duty 6x6 trucks.
Photo: REO Trucks White Motor Company acquired REO in 1957 and merged it with Diamond T in 1967 to form Diamond Reo Trucks. The operations in Lansing eventually closed following bankruptcy in 1975. Independent firms continued to produce heavy rigs under the REO name until 1995.
Now, REO is back with a bang and with three vehicles that threaten to ruin the plans of Ford and Slate. Its lineup starts with the base T4X Work Truck, a two-door, two-seat single-cab pickup with a steel drop-side flatbed, measuring 196.5 inches (4,991 millimeters) in length.
This model will hit the market with a target price of $21,500. In the meantime, the Slate Truck kicks off $24,950 (excluding a $1,450 destination charge), while Ford will ask $29,945 for its upcoming Fathom starting next year.
Higher up in the range will sit the T4C Crew Cab, a four-door, five-seat vehicle, featuring an extendable tailgate and the same wheelbase as the T4X, while it is slightly shorter (195.6 inches or 4,968 millimeters ). However, the load bed shrinks by 25 inches (635 millimeters), from 79.1 to 54.1 inches (from 2,009 to 1,374 millimeters). This one will start at $25,000.
Photo: REO Trucks The S4C Family SUV will sit at the top of the lineup. The off-road-focused boxy SUV will feature four doors and will carry up to six occupants in a cabin with a layout that integrates a three-seat second-row bench and a single side-facing jump seat.
All three models share a welded stamped-steel ladder frame, mechanical part-time 4WD, and a naturally aspirated inline-four gasoline engine paired with either the standard six-speed manual or the optional automatic transmission.
Just like the Slate pickup truck, the REO models come with zero touchscreens and no software-locked parts in favor of physical switches. Three HVAC knobs, a mechanical lever handbrake, and a standard DIN-style head unit slot will be on board as standard. A $30 diagnostic scanner and components that can be removed in under five minutes will be available to customers.
REO also announced an off-road Ransom package, which brings all-terrain tires, upgraded shocks, and a 2.5-inch lift. The Trail Wagon package will upgrade the off-road capabilities of the models, while the Speed Wagon will enhance performance.
Reservations are already open. All customers have to do is place a $25 refundable deposit. Pilot builds are scheduled to roll out in 2027. First customer deliveries are targeted for late 2028 or 2029.

XPENG G6 Electric Mid-Size Crossover SUV Goes Live in Australia, Starts From AU $49,990 Drive-Away
13 photos
Photo: Xpeng
The XPeng G6 is a battery-electric mid-size crossover SUV produced by the Chinese electric car company since 2023; now it makes its way into Australia , aka the Land Down Under, starting from the equivalent of about $33,633 at the current exchange rate.
XPENG Motors Australia is the local arm of XPeng Inc., responsible for sales, service, and “the ownership experience” in Australia and New Zealand, all through an expanding network of authorized dealers and service partners. The parent company is actually called Guangzhou Xiaopeng Motors Technology Co., Ltd., and was founded in 2014, with its current headquarters in Guangzhou, China, but also with offices in Mountain View, California, United States, and Munich, Germany.
It has described itself as a worldwide AI mobility technology company and researches and develops in-house technologies like full-stack advanced driver-assistance systems, intelligent car operating systems, powertrain systems, as well as vehicle electronic/electrical architectures. It currently manufactures one minivan and three passenger car models along with seven crossover and SUV nameplates.
Over in Australia, XPENG ANZ has recently announced an expansion of its current dealership and service network, which is set to include 66 locations across Victoria, New South Wales, Queensland, Western Australia, South Australia, and the Northern Territory by the end of December 2026. New Zealand buyers will also have access to XPENG models at seven locations.
Alongside the broader dealer and service network, XPENG also announced the upcoming L03 compact SUV and the G9L premium large SUV’s prices, which start from AU $41,900 ($28,207) for the smaller model. The other model available in Australia is the XPENG X9 luxury people mover , priced from AU $89,900 or $60,527 at the current exchange rate.
The XPENG G9L, their “large SUV for the AI era,” was revealed at the 2026 Paris Motor Show in early October in France, and the company promised that pricing information for the Australian market will arrive before the end of the year. However, now they’re focusing on a different model – the XPENG G6, which is now available in Australia priced from AU $49,990 drive-away (or almost $34k) across the Land Down Under.
The XPENG G6 RWD Standard Range is the base model featuring 185 kW and 440 Nm (248 hp and 325 lb-ft) of torque along with a 68.5 kWh LFP battery pack that enables a WLTP range of up to 480 km or 298 miles. It also has a max DC charging power of 382 kW, so it charges from 10 to 80% in 12 minutes. There are two more versions: the G6 RWD Long Range and the G6 AWD Long Range Performance.
The former starts from AU $55,990 or almost $38k and comes with 218 kW (292 hp) and a larger 80.8 kWh LFP battery pack, which is enough for a WLTP range of up to 525 km (326 miles). It also recharges in 12 minutes thanks to higher DC input at 451 kW. GM Ran 92,000 Virtual Crash Tests While Developing the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500
31 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
The Silverado 1500 has a bit of catching up to do in terms of crash protection. As far as the 2026 model is concerned, which is the final year of the previous generation, the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety gave the crew-cabbed truck a 'poor' rating in the moderate overlap test, with said result calling attention to rear occupant protection.
With the redesigned 2027 model, General Motors has taken a much deeper look at crash performance while developing the half-ton pickup. The Detroit-based automaker confirmed that no fewer than 92,000 virtual crash tests have been simulated before sending prototypes into physical barriers.
While there is no confirmed link to speak of between the outgoing truck's IIHS ratings and the scale of GM's simulation program, there is no denying that Detroit's largest automaker used Insurance Institute for Highway Safety data to improve the next-gen 'Rado. Truth be told, nearly 2 petabytes of data is a truly impressive amount of simulation work.
Before going any further, it's utmost important to highlight that General Motors hasn't abandoned physical testing. One of the real-world tests described by the Big G in the attached media release is the updated moderate overlap front crash test, with GM describing a truck hitting a barrier at 40 miles per hour (64 kilometers per hour) with 40 percent of its width on the driver's side.
The GM-described test further involves a 50th-percentile male dummy, which stands for the statistical median male, and a 5th-percentile female dummy. The smaller of the two dummies is seated in the rear, right behind the male driver, because smaller occupants face the highest risks of injury due to submarining and the worrying lack of rear pretensioners and load limiters in many modern vehicles. Said crash test dummy also mirrors the build of a small child.
Photo: Chevrolet General Motors evaluated hundreds of variations of the Silverado 1500's structure and passenger restraint system for this particular crash scenario, and doing it virtually in the first phase is a lot cheaper than destroying actual prototype trucks. Those hundreds of variations can also involve details that do not look particularly significant in isolation. Think material thickness, the way components are joined, and all that jazz. The restraint system obviously adds plenty other variables.
Simply put, simulating crash tests before getting down to business in the physical world is certain to have made the 2027 model year Silverado 1500 safer than its predecessor. GM claims that around 80 percent of the passive safety engineering work on the redesigned half-ton pickup was completed virtually.
Per the IIHS , full-size trucks don't consistently impress the nonprofit organization in relevant crashworthiness evaluations. The moderate overlap front test is a bit of an Achilles' heel for this kind of vehicle, with the Ford F-150 and Ram 1500 also scoring 'poor' in said evaluation. The Toyota Tundra, by comparison, earned a 'good' rating from the institute's safety boffins for model year 2026.
GM cites advancements in computer-aided design and engineering, along with advancements in simulation, for much of the work performed by its safety engineers in the virtual space. Artificial intelligence also had a role, enabling safety engineers to analyze more variations more quickly than ever before, helping them arrive at informed decisions sooner than previous digital toolkits.
“Virtual models help us explore more possibilities and refine the design; physical tests then confirm those results and help us improve the models," said Regina Carto, vice prez of Global Product Safety, Systems, and Certification at GM.
